Given that the differential equation 

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}-3y=4\operatorname{cos}⁡x-5\operatorname{sin}⁡x
$$

has the complementary solution ${y}_{c}(x)=A{e}^{3x}$, find the particular solution ${y}_{p}(x)$ to this equation.

${y}_{p}(x)=$
{{field-1}}
feedback.worked_solution:
To find the general solution of an inhomogeneous first-order linear equation with constant coefficients on the left-hand side, we must find the sum of the complementary and particular solutions.

The right-hand side of the inhomogeneous equation is $4\operatorname{cos}⁡x-5\operatorname{sin}⁡x.$ So, we assume the particular solution to be 

$$
{y}_{p}(x)=\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡x+\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡x,
$$

where $\alpha $ and $\beta $ are constants to be determined. 

Calculating the first derivative of ${y}_{p}$ gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}{y}_{p}}{\text{d}x}=-\alpha \operatorname{sin}⁡x+\beta \operatorname{cos}⁡x.
$$

To find the values of $\alpha $ and $\beta ,$ we substitute ${y}_{p}$ and ${y}_{p}^{′}$ into the differential equation:

$$
(-\alpha \operatorname{sin}⁡x+\beta \operatorname{cos}⁡x)-3(\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡x+\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡x)=4\operatorname{cos}⁡x-5\operatorname{sin}⁡x.
$$

Grouping the terms on the left-hand side gives

$$
(\beta -3\alpha )\operatorname{cos}⁡x-(\alpha +3\beta )\operatorname{sin}⁡x=4\operatorname{cos}⁡x-5\operatorname{sin}⁡x.
$$

Equating the coefficients, we get the following system of equations:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}\beta -3\alpha =4\, & (\text{equating the coefficients of}\,\operatorname{cos}⁡x) \\ \alpha +3\beta =5\, & (\text{equating the coefficients of}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡x)\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Solving this system gives: $\alpha =-\frac{7}{10},$ $\beta =\frac{19}{10}.$

Therefore, the particular solution ${y}_{p}(x)$ is

$$
{y}_{p}(x)=-\frac{7}{10}\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)+\frac{19}{10}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x).
$$
